## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater green alga belonging to the desmids, characterized by relatively large cells divided into two symmetrical, broadly pyramidal semicells by a deep central constriction. Euastrum didelta has strongly undulating margins, a deep notch at the apex of each semicell, and undivided basal lobes that help distinguish it from similar species. It occurs mainly in acidic to moderately nutrient-poor freshwater habitats such as ponds, bog pools, and shallow lakes. Like many desmids, it is associated with relatively clean, low-nutrient waters and contributes to freshwater primary production.
